subject: Hiding one of multiple legend keys?

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Hiding one of multiple legend keys?
parts:
I have a graph where my data is grouped by two variables. One of the variables is mapped to shape, and the other is mapped to the color fill. The variable that's mapped to shape is also used for faceting. Is there a way to remove the legend key for just that one variable? It is redundant in this case.

In this example, the variable in question is "group1":

library(ggplot2)
n <- 60
data <- data.frame(
    x = rnorm(n),
    y = rnorm(n)
    group1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), n, replace=TRUE)
    group2 = sample(c("L","M"), n, replace=TRUE) )

ggplot(data=data, aes(x=x, y=y, shape=group1, fill=group2)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_shape_manual(values=c(21,24,22)) +
    facet_grid(group1 ~ .)

Normally, to remove a legend key, you use opts(legend.position='none'), but in this case it removes both legends, which isn't desirable.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Hiding one of multiple legend keys?
parts:
Hi:

Try this:

n <- 60
dat <- data.frame(
x = rnorm(n),
y = rnorm(n),
group1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), n, replace=TRUE),

ggplot(data=dat, aes(x=x, y=y, shape = group1, fill=group2)) +
geom_point() +
scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(dat$group1),
values = c(21, 24, 22),
legend = FALSE) +
facet_grid(group1 ~ .)

HTH,
Dennis

Actually, I just noticed another issue with the graph. The code works perfectly -- it's just that the legend shows colored circles, which may convey the (erroneous) idea that the legend only applies to group A, which uses circles. Groups B and C use triangles and squares, but the legend should apply to them as well.

It would be ideal if it were possible to make the legend have solid colors without the circles at all, or perhaps if it could have large square points (that don't quite fill the entire box) filled with the appropriate color. Is it possible to control the point shape and size inside the legend?

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Hiding one of multiple legend keys?
parts:
Hi,

in the next version, you can do this:

n <- 60
dat <- data.frame(
x = rnorm(n),
y = rnorm(n),
group1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), n, replace=TRUE),
group2 = sample(c("L","M"), n, replace=TRUE) )

ggplot(data=dat, aes(x=x, y=y, shape = group1, fill=group2)) +
geom_point() +
scale_shape_manual(breaks = levels(dat$group1),
values = c(21, 24, 22),
legend = FALSE) +

guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 10, shape = 22))) +
facet_grid(group1 ~ .)


--
